senses.gloss: f. (πομπή, pompa) solemn procession, pomp, solemnity, ostentation.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 1:1:5">Y. Shek. I, beg. 45ᵈ</cite> <he>כדי לעשות פומבי לדבר</he> (Ms. M. <he>פוספי</he>, read <cite ref="Q00254"><he>פומפי</he></cite>) in order to give greater publicity to the act; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 2:1:18">Y. Yoma II, 39ᵈ</cite> top; ib. II, end, 40ᵃ; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 12:1">Pesik. R. s. 12</cite> <he>לפי שלא נעשית לה פ׳ כאמהות</he> because she had not been given a public funeral as was given to the other Mothers.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 5:1">Ib. s. 5</cite> <he>עשה להם פומבה גדולה</he> made a great demonstration for them.
<cite ref="Bava Batra 145b:6">B. Bath. 145ᵇ</cite> <he>עשה עמו בפ׳ וכ׳</he> if a man acted as a friend’s best man at a public wedding, and now asks his friend to be his best man at a private wedding.
Ib. עתיר נכסין עתיר פ׳ וכ׳ rich in goods, rich in pomp (popular ovations)—that is the preacher of hagadah (v. אֲגָדָה); a. fr.—Trnsf. (v. Sophocles s. v. πομπή) disgrace, reproach.

<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 54b:17">Ab. Zar. 54ᵇ</cite> <he>לא דיין … שעושין סלע שלי פ׳ וכ׳</he> it is not enough for the wicked that they have made my coin (divine image of man) a public disgrace, but &c.—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 86:2">Gen. R. s. 86</cite>, beg. <he>בני בכורי הוא ואני מורידו פורופי</he> Ar. (read: <cite ref="Q00254"><he>פומפי</he></cite> = πομπῇ) he (Jacob) is my firstborn son, and shall I let him go down to Egypt in disgrace?—Ed. <he>בני … בבזיון ואם ליתן בלבו של פרעה איני מורידו פומבי אלא וכ׳</he> (corr. after ‘Rashi’ <he>ואם אתן בלבו … להורידו איני מורידו פ׳</he>) he is my firstborn son, and shall I make him go down in contempt? and if I put it into Pharaoh’s heart to bring him down, do I not bring him down in disgrace? (‘Rashi’ <he>אני מורידו פופילא</he>, corr. acc.).
